newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian security frees oil community chief.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian security frees oil community chief.

text.p: The leader of a restive oil-producing community held over a deadline he set for the Nigerian unit of oil giant Shell to pay compensation or leave said he had been freed.

Matthew Eregbeng, president of the Niger Delta Oil-Producing Development Organisation told reporters in the oil town of Warri on Thursday that he was freed by security authorities following the intervention of the midwestern Delta state government.
Eregbeng was arrested on Tuesday as the deadline by four ethnic Ijaw communities to Shell to pay the compensation or be forced out of their oil-producing areas expired.
He said he and other community leaders would meet Shell officials on Monday in Asaba, Delta state capital, to try to resolve the problem.
"The meeting is at the instance of the Delta state government and until then we are staying any action against Shell," Eregbeng said.

The four communities recently won a tussle against Shell in local courts over compensation of around 30 million naira ($353,000) for environmental damage, but say Shell is planning to appeal to a higher court.
Shell maintains that it is acting within its legal rights to appeal and says the spillage involved was proven to have been caused by sabotage.

Ethnic clashes in March between Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen in the Warri area killed scores of people and forced Shell to close several oil wells earlier this year after fighting erupted over the relocation of a local government headquarters.
Shell pumps around half of the nation's roughly two million bpd crude oil production.
